key_insight: Solution-phase ligand exchange enables thicker AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers with efficient charge extraction, supporting 24.0%-efficient four-terminal perovskite tandems.
engineering_relevance: One-step deposition of passivated AgBiS2 nanocrystals offers a route toward scalable near-infrared sub-cells for thin-film tandem photovoltaics.
method: Model tandem performance using the experimental AgBiS2 absorption spectrum.
Use solution-phase ligand exchange to enable an order-of-magnitude increase in absorber thickness.
Integrate AgBiS2 with visible-light-absorbing perovskites in four-terminal and monolithic tandems.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 24.0% four-terminal tandem efficiency, voltage addition in monolithic tandems, and >90% efficiency retention after three months of unencapsulated dry-air storage; triple-junction efficiencies above 47.5% are modeled, not demonstrated.
watch_item: Dry-air storage stability does not establish operational durability under illumination, heat, or humidity.
paper_title: AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics
